analysis: What changed versus the 4:00 AM brief: the bounce broadened and firmed. Futures strengthened further (Nasdaq +1.93% vs +1.68% at 4 AM, S&P +0.87% vs +0.79%), and the rally spread beyond Nvidia into the whole chip and optical complex — Micron ~+7%, AMD and Intel +6%+, SK Hynix and SanDisk +8%+, Lumentum/Credo/Coherent ~+9%. CoreWeave is now +12-13% premarket (vs +10.8% at 4 AM), with Nebius +11.4% and Iren +7.9% riding along. Nvidia itself cooled a touch from its +5.3% early peak to +4.0% ($175.65) — still relief, still trading the House deadline due today, not the Nov 17 print. The offsetting pressure also rose: Brent pushed to $92.51 (+1.11%) and briefly $93.61 after fresh Hormuz tanker incidents, and the EIA's Nov 10 outlook has Brent averaging ~$100 in Nov-Dec, so the energy risk premium is rebuilding even as equities rally. Nothing about the rate problem changed — a December hike is still near-certain (~90%), the 10-year is parked at 4.983%, and the bond market stays closed for Veterans Day. BofA's 'S&P 500 is the world's most crowded trade' warning for 2027 is the counterweight to the morning's risk-on tone. Signal vs noise: the chip-wide breadth and CoreWeave's raised outlook are signal that the AI-capex fear is easing at the margin; the Hormuz mine claim (Iranian military, unverified by AP) is the fragile detail inside an otherwise confirmed oil move; BofA's 2027 call is positioning color, not a near-term driver. The open's test is whether the Nasdaq's near-2% futures lead holds without bonds to validate it, and whether Nvidia answers the House today.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures extended the overnight bounce: as of ~11:46 UTC (Longbridge), S&P 500 futures +0.87%, Nasdaq-100 futures +1.93%, Dow futures +0.13%. European markets also higher (DAX +0.45%, FTSE +0.33%, CAC +0.25%). Tuesday's close: S&P 500 7,520.93 (-0.38%), Nasdaq 25,065.88 (-0.74%), Dow 52,231.89 (-0.30%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The relief rally firmed into the morning — the Nasdaq lead widened from +1.68% at 4 AM to +1.93% — but the rate backdrop that caused Tuesday's slide has not changed.

headlines.headline: Nvidia +4.00% premarket to $175.65 as of 7:52 AM ET (Finnhub), easing from a +5.3% peak earlier in the session, after falling 4.27% Monday and 5.47% Tuesday to close at $168.89 — a two-session loss of roughly $480B and a five-session slide of -16.4%. Today is the deadline for CEO Jensen Huang to reply to three House chairmen seeking a closed-door briefing (proposed Nov 18); no public reply had surfaced as of this morning. NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17 (expected EPS $2.53, revenue $111.4B).
headlines.why_it_matters: Relief after the steepest governance-driven slide in years, but the stock is still trading the congressional timeline, not the Nov 17 print — and the bounce has already cooled from its early high.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave (CRWV) now +12-13% premarket (Longbridge, Upstox) after Q3 revenue of $3,661M beat estimates and the company raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $13.0-13.3B (vs $12.86B LSEG estimate), saying it expects to become profitable on an adjusted basis in the first half of 2028. Peers followed: Nebius +11.4%, Iren +7.9% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The neocloud name was the epicenter of AI-spending and debt fears, so a beat plus a raised outlook and a profitability date is the single biggest sentiment input into the open — and it is lifting the whole AI complex with it.

headlines.headline: The chip and optical rally broadened premarket: SK Hynix and SanDisk +8%+, Seagate and Western Digital +7%+, Micron ~+7%, AMD and Intel +6%+, Broadcom +4%+, Qualcomm +3%+; Lumentum, Credo and Coherent ~+9%, Marvell +8%+, Astera Labs and Corning +7%+ (Longbridge).
headlines.why_it_matters: Breadth across semis and opticals shows the move is not just a Nvidia short-cover — the AI-hardware complex is being re-bought as a group after the CoreWeave print.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mixed-to-higher premarket (Finnhub / Stock Market Watch, ~7:52-7:53 AM ET): TSLA +1.70% to $386.25, GOOG +1.1% to $288.11, META +0.8% to $646.65, MSFT +0.39% to $535.22, AMZN +0.2% to $271.30, AAPL -0.54% to $346.61. Tesla reported Q3 FY2026 on Oct 21 (EPS $0.48, revenue $28.05B); Apple reported Q4 FY2026 on Nov 2 (EPS $2.10, revenue $114.48B); Microsoft reported Q1 FY2027 on Oct 28 (EPS $4.89, revenue $92.28B).
headlines.why_it_matters: Most megacaps are riding the futures bounce, with Tesla the strongest of the group; Apple is the lone decliner, giving back a little of its recent strength.

headlines.headline: Oil climbed further on Hormuz shipping attacks: Brent $92.51 (+1.11%) and WTI $86.61 (+0.8%) by 04:20 GMT, with Brent briefly touching $93.61 after reports of a tanker hitting a naval mine. UKMTO confirmed a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile northeast of Lima, Oman, on Tuesday; Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines — a claim AP could not independently verify. The EIA's Nov 10 outlook has Brent averaging ~$100 in Nov-Dec; API data showed US crude inventories up ~9M barrels in the week ended Nov 6.
headlines.why_it_matters: A rising supply-risk premium in crude works against the equity bounce — and the mine detail inside the story is single-source and unverified, so treat that part as fragile even though the price move and the UKMTO strike are confirmed.

headlines.headline: Bank of America: the S&P 500 is the world's most crowded trade and may struggle as a foundation for bullish positions in 2027 (Longbridge summary). Goldman Sachs also adjusted its Fed hiking-cycle forecast after Tuesday's hot CPI print.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source analyst color, but it frames the tension in the tape: a crowded index rallying into a near-certain December hike, with the 10-year just under 5%.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. The fresh angle is crude: WTI $86.61 (+0.8%) and Brent $92.51 premarket after the Hormuz incidents, which steadies the energy backdrop. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.1M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, ~$0.03 beat), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M.
